nodes.name: Nickel foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: The nickel foam was ultrasonically cleaned with HCl and deionized water for 5.0 min to remove external impurities and oxides, respectively.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, the nickel foam was ultrasonically cleaned with HCl and deionized water for 5.0 min to remove external impurities and oxides, respectively.

nodes.name: NCF-precursor hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1.0 mmol of Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 1.0 mmol of Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 0.20 mmol of Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O, 5.0 mmol of NH₄F, and 10.0 mmol of urea were mixed in 50.0 ml of deionized water and stirred to gain homogeneous solution. Then, the above solution and nickel foam were put into a Teflon-lined autoclave with the capacity of 100.0 mL for hydrothermal reaction at 120.0°C for 6.0 h. Subsequently, the solution after thermal treatment was rinsed with deionized water several times and dried at 60.0°C, and the obtained product was denoted as NCF-precursor.

nodes.name: NCFP phosphorization
nodes.procedure: The phosphorization process was executed in a quartz tube reactor heated by horizontal furnace. The NaH₂PO₂·H₂O powders and NCF-precursor were located in the upstream and downstream of the gas flow, respectively. The horizontal tube furnace was heated to 300.0°C and kept for 2.0 h under the protection of the Ar atmosphere. After natural cooling down, the product of NiCoFeP (NCFP) nanowires was achieved. The mass loading of NCFP is about 3.0 mg cm⁻².

nodes.name: NCFP@LDH electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: LDH nanosheets were prepared using Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O and Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O as precursors. In a standard three-electrode electrochemical system, LDH nanosheets were electrodeposited on the prepared NCFP nanowires, where the NCFP nanowires on nickel foam, Pt foil, and Ag/AgCl were used as the working electrode, counter electrode, and reference electrode, respectively. Electrodeposition was performed at a constant voltage of -1.0 V for 200.0 s. After electrodeposition, the resulting composite electrode was washed several times with deionized water and ethanol and dried at 70.0°C in air. The obtained product was denoted as NCFP@LDH. The mass loading of NCFP@LDH... is about 4.0 mg cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows nanowire topography with rough surface and nanosheets on nanowire surface confirming NCFP@LDH core-shell structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM image in Fig. 2b shows the morphology of the synthesized sample, in which the nanowire topography can be clearly observed... SEM investigations at higher magnification (Fig. 2c) show that there are nanosheets on the surface of the nanowires, which suggests the formation of NCFP@LDH core-shell structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms NCFP nanowire covered by ultrathin LDH nanosheets; HRTEM shows (111) crystal plane of NiCoFeP and amorphous LDH with no long-range lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2d shows a typical brightfield TEM of the NCFP@LDH... high-resolution TEM image and the corresponding fast Fourier transform (FFT) pattern were shown in Fig. 2e... Fig. 2f shows the high-resolution TEM at the interface between NiCoFeP and LDH, and it can be seen that there is no long-range lattice in the LDH nanosheet.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mappings show Ni, Co, Fe uniformly distributed in nanowire and nanosheet; P only in internal nanowire.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mappings (Fig. 2g) show that Ni, Co, and Fe are uniformly distributed in both the internal nanowire and the external nanosheet while the P element is only distributed in the internal nanowire.

nodes.characterization_summary: NCFP shows diffraction peaks at 40.6°, 44.4°, 47.3° for (111), (201), (201) planes of NiCoP; LDH amorphous with no obvious peaks; NCFP@LDH matches NCFP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern in Fig. 3a shows the diffraction peaks of NCFP at 40.6°, 44.4°, and 47.3° corresponding to the (111), (201) and (201) planes of NiCoP... The XRD pattern of LDH sample does not show obvious diffraction peak.

nodes.characterization_summary: NCFP@LDH shows M-OH characteristic peaks at 465.0 cm^{-1}, 518.0 cm^{-1}, 648.0 cm^{-1} confirming LDH formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on the compared Raman spectra in Fig. 3b, NCFP@LDH shows the characteristic peaks M-OH (M = Ni, Fe, Co) at 465.0 cm^{-1}, 518.0 cm^{-1} and 648.0 cm^{-1} which suggests the formation of LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows -OH peaks at 3217.0 cm^{-1} (stretching) and 1646.0 cm^{-1} (bending) confirming LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FTIR spectra in Fig. 3c shows the characteristic peaks of -OH at around 3217.0 cm^{-1} and 1646.0 cm^{-1} in which the broad band at 3217.0 cm^{-1} can be attributed to the stretching vibration of the hydroxyl groups in the LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Ni, Co, Fe, P, O; shows shifted binding energies indicating electron transfer: Ni 2p3/2 Ni-O at 856.10 eV, Co 2p3/2 Co-O at 781.70 eV (shifted lower), Fe 2p Fe3+ at 712.60 eV (shifted higher); P 2p P-M at 129.60/130.90 eV, PO4^3- at 134.30 eV; O 1s oxide/hydroxy at 530.20/531.10 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The wide-scan XPS spectrum in Fig. 3d confirms the presence of Ni, Co, Fe, P, and O elements in NCFP@LDH. The Ni 2p3/2 spectrum (Fig. 3e) can be divided into two peaks of Ni-O (856.10 eV)... the electron binding energy corresponding to M-O was shifted to the direction of low binding energies (M = Ni, Co). The peak (712.60 eV) in Fig. 3g suggests the existence of Fe3+, and the electron binding energy in NCFP@LDH was shifted to higher binding energy compared to that of NCFP.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at non-faradaic potentials (5-25 mV/s) used to calculate Cdl = 192.77 mF cm^{-2} for NCFP@LDH (HER), indicating high ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To estimate the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) of the active materials, CV tests were performed at the scan rate of 5.0~25.0 mV/s... Detailed calculations (Fig. 4e) show that the Cdl of NCFP@LDH, NCFP, and LDH is 192.77 mF cm^{-2}, 73.20 mF cm^{-2}, and 13.77 mF cm^{-2}, respectively.
